title: Analysis of methanol and ethanol in virgin olive oil
author: Gómez-Coca, Cruz-Hidalgo, et al.

steps.title: Prepare spiked calibration samples
steps.instruction: Take the in‑house blank refined olive‑pomace oil and add methanol (MeOH), ethanol (EtOH) and propanol (PrOH, internal standard) to obtain concentrations between 4 mg kg⁻¹ and 12 mg kg⁻¹ for each analyte. Mix thoroughly and verify that each resulting peak has a signal‑to‑noise ratio of at least 3, is sharp, symmetrical and shows no tailing or shoulders.

steps.title: Prepare LOD and LOQ spike series
steps.instruction: Spike eleven separate aliquots of the same refined olive‑pomace oil with MeOH, EtOH and PrOH standard solutions at decreasing concentrations ranging from 992.1 mg kg⁻¹ down to 0.02 mg kg⁻¹. Perform each concentration in duplicate and confirm that peaks are sharp, symmetrical, have signal‑to‑noise ≥ 2 and exhibit no tailing or shoulders.

steps.title: Perform static headspace extraction
steps.instruction: Place each oil sample (calibration, LOD/LOQ, and unknown virgin olive oil) in a sealed headspace vial, equilibrate under the laboratory’s standard static‑headspace conditions for short‑chain alcohols, and collect the headspace gas for injection.

steps.title: Run GC‑FID analysis
steps.instruction: Inject the collected headspace aliquot into a gas chromatograph equipped with a flame‑ionisation detector (GC‑FID). Use the method that yields three distinct peaks for MeOH, EtOH and PrOH with absolute retention times measured to three decimal places and constant relative retention times across runs.

steps.title: Apply detector response correction
steps.instruction: Because the FID response for PrOH is 1.32‑fold lower than for MeOH and 1.43‑fold lower than for EtOH, correct the peak areas: divide the MeOH area by 1.32 and the EtOH area by 1.43 (or equivalently multiply the PrOH area by these factors) before quantitative calculations.

steps.title: Calculate volatile concentrations
steps.instruction: For each analyte compute its concentration (mg kg⁻¹) using the formula: Concentration = (Ax × mIS) / (AIS × mS), where Ax is the corrected peak area of the analyte, AIS is the peak area of PrOH, mIS is the mass of PrOH added to the sample (mg), and mS is the mass of the oil sample used for the determination (g).

steps.title: Report results with LOD/LOQ limits
steps.instruction: Report a concentration only if it is ≥ 0.55 mg kg⁻¹ (limit of detection) and ≥ 0.59 mg kg⁻¹ (limit of quantitation). Values below these thresholds are considered not quantifiable.
